findings.issue: The read cache can keep serving a page rendered from the user's row as it was before a committed change to that user. Authentication loads the signed-in user first (Concerns.fs:158, through ReadCache.user), and only later does ReadCache.page take the version counters (ReadCache.fs:205, roomDeps at :234, userRoomsDeps at :238). The page is rendered from the user object authentication loaded. If a change to that user commits and its counters are released between those two points, the page is built from the old row but stored under the new counter values. It is then served to every later request until an unrelated write moves a counter. The pages hit are the room page (current-user-name meta tag and the composer's message template), the sidebar (name, avatar, and the administrator-only New Chat Room button) and the search page, which has the same layout. This breaks plan rule 2: a stale page after a committed write, by the same user and, for role changes, by an admin.
findings.evidence:
Scratch tests A1, A1b and A1c each make 1,500 writes; after each write returns, a fresh request is checked while 12 other browsers read the same page.
- A1, self-rename, room page: 93 and 75 stale pages in two runs. Example: after the rename to 'David 5' committed, the page still showed meta and template 'David 4', and the next request with no write in between showed 'David 4' again.
- A1b, sidebar name: 50 stale.
- A1c, restricted seed, role toggled by SQL: 79 sidebars disagreed with the committed role. Some showed New Chat Room after David became Member; others hid it after he became Administrator.
- With CAMPFIRE_READ_CACHE=off, all three tests found 0 stale pages, so the cache causes it.
- With CAMPFIRE_GROUP_COMMIT=off and the cache on, the room page and sidebar tests still fail, so group commit is not the cause.
- Logs: scratchpad/attack/a1-cache-on.log, a1-cache-off.log, a1c-on.log, a1c-off.log.
findings.fix: Take the global counter value at the moment authentication loads the user, and use that value as the page's global dependency, so the page is neither stored nor served if a change to users happened in between. The users cache entry already holds this value as its Dep. Alternatively, take the page's counters before beforeActions runs, or add the user's updated_at to the cache key. Add A1, A1b and A1c to ReadCacheTests.

findings.issue: Memory grows without bound with the room ids that signed-in users put in URLs. Versions.Room (line 67) calls rooms.GetOrAdd for any id. ReadCache.roomDeps (ReadCache.fs:234) calls it with the room id parsed from the URL before set_room checks that the room exists or that the user is a member. Cells are never removed, so any signed-in user can add one cell per request for /rooms/N or /rooms/N/messages with a new N.
findings.evidence: Scratch test A2: 40,000 requests for room ids that do not exist, half to /rooms/N and half to /rooms/N/messages, every one answered 302 or 404. The room version cells went from 0 to 40,000. The managed heap kept 587 bytes per request, against 392 with CAMPFIRE_READ_CACHE=off, so about 195 bytes per distinct id. Extrapolated, 10 million ids would hold about 2 GB. Logs: scratchpad/attack/a2.log and a2-off.log.
findings.fix: Create a room cell only once the room is known to exist and the user is a member: on a miss, take the cell after set_room succeeds, but keep the rule that counters are read before the first query. Or use a fixed-size array of counters indexed by a hash of the room id, where a collision only causes extra invalidation. Or skip caching for a room id that has no cell yet.

findings.issue: Group commit more than doubles how often concurrent posts are broadcast out of commit order. The writer answers every caller in a group one after another (Database.fs:712). Each request then broadcasts from its own continuation in messages#create (Messages.fs:432), so posts committed together go out in whatever order their continuations happen to run. The port reorders too, but much less. For appends this cannot be seen: the client re-sorts appended messages by data-sort-value (reference messages_controller.js:175-188), and created_at follows commit order inside a group. A replace and a remove of the same message from requests that are in flight at the same time are not re-sorted.
findings.evidence:
Scratch test A5: 16 browsers each post 20 messages to All Talk, while a raw Hub subscriber records the data-message-id of each broadcast.
- Group commit on: 100, 92, 93 and 95 adjacent inversions out of 319 pairs over four runs.
- CAMPFIRE_GROUP_COMMIT=off: 40, 49, 38 and 33.
- All 320 broadcasts arrived every time, with no lag.
- Logs: scratchpad/attack/a45-on.log, a45-off.log, a5-reps.log.
findings.fix: If the order matters, send a message's broadcast as an after-commit event on the writer, so events go out in commit order, or have the client ignore a replace that is older than what it has (data-message-updated-at). Otherwise, record in oncrack-c2.md that group commit increases broadcast reordering and that clients re-sort appends.

findings.issue: bin/kit-differential http now exits 1 by default. Since C3, every gzipped buffer and frozen page carries a Content-Length, which Rust's kit does not send. This difference is deliberate and the bodies are identical, but the gate fails unless it is run with CAMPFIRE_GZIP_LENGTH=off. That turns off the code path being shipped, so the shipped path no longer has a header differential.
findings.evidence: With default settings: plain 1,500 requests, 181 differ; ssl 1,500 requests, 82 differ. Every difference shown is only an added ('content-length', N), on 200, 404 and other statuses. With CAMPFIRE_GZIP_LENGTH=off: 0 differ in both. Logs: scratchpad/kithttp.log and kithttp-off.log.
findings.fix: Make reference-tools/kit/http-differential/fuzz.py accept a content-length on gzip answers from the F# side when it equals the body's length, and fail on every other difference. Record the deliberate difference where onCrack's differences are listed.
